body:
The memo added in #1404 (cps/epub.py) caches only successful parses, including the common
"no rendition:layout" result. The `except` path returns None WITHOUT caching (cps/epub.py:85-87).

So a corrupt or unreadable EPUB re-opens, re-parses and re-logs an error line every time it is
emitted in a sync page, forever. That is pre-#1404 behaviour for that book so it is not a
regression, but the cache was the natural place to cap it, and the log spam is unbounded.

Fix: cache the failure under the same key. An mtime or size change already invalidates the entry,
so a repaired file is picked up automatically.

Also worth recording about that cache, both by design rather than defects:
- The bound is 4096 entries and a sync walks the library in `(last_modified, id)` order, so a
  library larger than 4096 books gets close to a 0% hit rate across a full sync. The measured
  "400ms -> 11ms per page" figure is a <=4096-book number. The CHANGELOG was corrected to say so.
- On NFS/SMB every call still pays one `os.stat` on the greenlet — a network round trip per book
  — so the win there is real but smaller than the local-disk numbers.
title: EPUB layout cache does not remember failures, so a corrupt book re-parses and re-logs on every sync page
